newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Madagascar's impeached president warns opponents.
newsitem.headline: Madagascar's impeached president warns opponents.

text.p: Madagascar's impeached president, Albert Zafy, told his opponents on Sunday to allow early elections by November 4 or run the risk of unrest.

"Disorder could occur if those in charge of the political transition fail to scrupulously respect the date laid down in the constitution for a new presidential election," Zafy said in a statement on state radio.
Zafy was referring to the provision that new elections must be held within 60 days of a president's death, resignation or impeachment.

The Indian Ocean island's constitutional court upheld his impeachment last week after parliament, controlled by his opponents, had voted for the extreme measure on the grounds that Zafy had repeatedly violated the constitution.

Zafy's Sunday statement was a reply to suggestions from the opposition, particularly by parliamentary speaker Richard Andriamanjato, that the presidential election might have to be deferred until after major constitutional amendments.
Zafy, who is not barred from running in the election, believes he will win so long as it is held promptly.

Zafy said on September 5 that he would step down as president on October 10. The constitutional court ordered Prime Minister Norbert Norbert Ratsirahonana to take over the duties of head of state until the elections.
But on Sunday Zafy said Ratsirahonana could not be considered as interim president and that he, Zafy, would only formally hand over his office to the victor in the polls.
The presidential polls were not due until 1998.
The impeachment capped three years of political instability since Zafy was elected in 1993 after a long and sometimes violent struggle for democracy by the 14 million islanders.

The squabbling has frustrated efforts to get the economy moving and the latest row may upset Madagascar's hopes of concluding new debt-rescheduling and lending agreements this month with the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.
